claims.text: The unmodified as-sintered tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure lacking engineered nanoprecipitates.
A fabrication thermal/process treatment can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The treatment produces coherent nanoprecipitates with well-defined interfaces in the tungsten-alloy matrix.
Introducing SCCPs will improve the radiation tolerance of tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced vacancies.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces capture helium atoms.
Capture of vacancies and helium at coherent interfaces limits helium-bubble growth and coalescence.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation motion or transmission.
Facilitating dislocation motion at coherent interfaces prevents irradiation-induced embrittlement.
SCCPs can preserve high strength and tensile ductility in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
After irradiation, the SCCP-treated alloy will maintain or enhance tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated control.
After helium irradiation, the SCCP-treated alloy will have lower helium-bubble density and size than the untreated control.
The SCCP-treated alloy will retain less deuterium and helium than the untreated control.
The proposed effect should hold under helium-ion bombardment at energies from tens to hundreds of keV and temperatures up to 800 °C.
The benefits require sintering routes that permit controlled coherent nanoprecipitate formation.
The benefits may not extend to fundamentally different alloy compositions.
The long-term stability of SCCPs under prolonged irradiation and extreme thermal cycling remains uncertain.
